title: QA and software testing

noc.title: Information systems testing technicians
noc.applies_when: Manual and automated software testing, test case design, defect management. The lane's home code.

noc.title: Software developers and programmers
noc.applies_when: SDET and test-automation-engineer seats where the body is mostly writing code. Stronger code, read the duties before claiming it.

noc.title: Information systems specialists
noc.applies_when: QA seats folded into a broader systems-analysis role.

skills.name: Test case design
skills.asked_for: Writing cases from requirements, positive and negative paths, boundary and equivalence

skills.name: Manual testing execution
skills.asked_for: Functional, regression, smoke, UAT support, cross-browser and cross-device
skills.evidence: Manual testing of his own builds across K2 client sites and personal projects. Not against a formal test plan or in a team QA process.
skills.limit: Not against a formal test plan or in a team QA process.

skills.name: Defect management
skills.asked_for: Reproduction steps, severity and priority, lifecycle through to retest and closure
skills.evidence: Issue tracking in his own GitHub repos. Not in Jira or an enterprise defect workflow.
skills.limit: Not in Jira or an enterprise defect workflow.

skills.name: Bug reporting quality
skills.asked_for: A report a developer can act on without a follow-up conversation
skills.evidence: Same as above, self-directed rather than reviewed.
skills.limit: Same as above, self-directed rather than reviewed.

skills.name: SDLC and Agile
skills.asked_for: Sprints, ceremonies, where QA sits in the cycle, definition of done

skills.name: Test management tooling
skills.asked_for: Jira, Azure DevOps, TestRail, Zephyr or similar

skills.name: API testing
skills.asked_for: Postman or equivalent, request and response validation, status codes, payload assertions
skills.evidence: Heavy API and JSON work across the n8n pipelines and K2_Press. Covers request and response handling, not a structured API test suite.
skills.limit: Covers request and response handling, not a structured API test suite.

skills.name: SQL for test data
skills.asked_for: Querying to set up and verify test state
skills.note: See lane 5, same gap, same fix.

skills.name: Test automation
skills.asked_for: Selenium, Playwright, Cypress. Playwright and Cypress dominate new postings

skills.name: Programming for automation
skills.asked_for: JavaScript or TypeScript or Python well enough to write and maintain tests
skills.evidence: React, Next.js, TypeScript and Node.js work across K2 builds; Python across the automation pipelines. The language is there, the testing framework is not.

skills.name: Git and CI
skills.asked_for: Branching, pull requests, tests running in a pipeline

skills.name: Mobile and responsive testing
skills.evidence: Responsive verification on client sites. Not on a device lab or emulator matrix.
skills.limit: Not on a device lab or emulator matrix.

skills.name: Performance testing
skills.asked_for: JMeter, k6. Rarely required at junior level

skills.name: Accessibility testing
skills.asked_for: WCAG, axe. Increasingly asked for in public-sector postings

skills.name: ISTQB Foundation
skills.asked_for: Not required, but it is the one certification that reliably moves a junior QA resume

skills.name: CI/CD pipeline ownership
skills.asked_for: Jenkins, GitHub Actions as the test owner rather than a user

positioning:
The truth today: he can read and write the code QA roles automate against, he handles APIs and JSON fluently, and he has tested his own work. What he has not done is QA inside a team, against a test plan, in a defect workflow, with a test management tool. That is the whole gap and it is a process gap, not an intelligence gap, which is worth saying plainly in a cover letter rather than hiding.

On current statuses most QA postings grade Tier B or Tier C. The fastest move to Tier A is Playwright or Cypress plus one public repo with a real test suite, and ISTQB Foundation if a run shows it appearing as a hard requirement more than occasionally. Lane 1 and lane 5 share the SQL gap, so closing SQL once moves both lanes.
interview_watch: QA screens are practical. Expect to be handed a feature and asked what you would test, and expect a follow-up on how you would prioritise when there is not time to test everything. Have an answer for both. Also expect "what is the difference between severity and priority", which is the single most common QA screening question.
pr_note: 22222 lost its BC PNP route when BC removed the priority technology list on 23 April 2026. AIP from a designated Atlantic employer is now the one designated pathway for this code, and an Ontario job offer qualifies under the Workforce Priority stream. Weight Atlantic and Ontario QA roles accordingly.
not_required: Security testing, penetration testing, and formal test strategy ownership. Those are senior seats and a posting that hard-requires them has failed the seniority gate anyway.
